data.headline: SPY’s Treasury spread narrowed as both benchmarks fell
data.summary: The ten-year minus two-year Treasury spread narrowed from 34 to 32 basis points between November 3 and 4. The ten-year yield fell by 5 basis points and the two-year by 3. Lower benchmarks and a narrower spread can affect borrowers and lenders differently across the S&P 500.

bull.text: The ten-year yield declined from 4.95% to 4.90%, and the two-year from 4.61% to 4.58%. Lower benchmark yields can ease financing or valuation assumptions when company credit spreads and expected cash flows hold fixed.

bear.text: The long-short Treasury spread narrowed by 2 basis points to 32. Lenders’ funding costs, asset repricing and credit losses determine how this curve change affects their margins.

watch.text: October 27 S&P futures positions show asset managers net long 923,449 contracts and leveraged funds net short 400,604. Their differing category balances predate the November yield changes.

limitations: The rates are dated November 4. SPY returns, constituent earnings revisions and company credit spreads remain unmeasured.
The related S&P futures report measures weekly contract positions. SPY fund flows, current investor intent and intraday options exposure require separate evidence.
